decision.explanation: The provided evidence (pmid-21796119) exclusively reports on somatic mutations in Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma (NHL), specifically identifying MLL2 and MEF2B as drivers in DLBCL and Follicular Lymphoma. The text contains no mention of breast adenocarcinoma, the EGFR gene, the L858R variant, or the drug Erlotinib. Therefore, the evidence is entirely irrelevant to the claim regarding EGFR L858R-mediated resistance to Erlotinib in breast adenocarcinoma.

citations.quote: "e approach proposed by Greenman et al. We reasoned that this would reveal genes with strong selection signatures, and mutations in such genes would be good candidate cancer drivers. We identified 26 genes with significant evidence for positive selection (FDR 0.03, Methods), with either selective pressure for acquiring non-synonymous point mutations or truncating/nonsense mutations (Methods; Table 1; Supplementary Table S8). Included were known lymphoma oncogenes (BCL2, CD79B, CARD11, MYD88 and EZH2), all of which exhibited signatures indicative of selection for non-synonymous

six additional variants outside exons 2 and 3. We thus identified 69 cases (34 DLBCL; 12.67% and 35 FL; 15.33%) with MEF2B cSNVs or indels, failing to observe novel variants in other NHL and non-malignant samples. 55 (80%) of the variants affected residues within the MADS box and MEF2 domains encoded by exons 2 and 3 (Supplementary Table S11; Figure 3B). Each patient generally had a single MEF2B variant and we observed relatively few (8 total, 10.7%) truncation-inducing SNVs or indels. Non-synonymous SNVs were by far the most common type of change observed, with 59.4% of detected variants
